title: BlueCo’s approach at Chelsea ‘yielding results’, says co-owner Jose E. Feliciano
content:
Chelsea co-owner Jose E. Feliciano has said BlueCo has implemented a “more sustainable system” that is “yielding results” at the club.

Feliciano is co-founder and managing partner — alongside Behdad Eghbali — of Clearlake Capital, the private equity firm leading the consortium BlueCo, which owns Chelsea.

The 53-year-old, speaking at business conference Bloomberg Invest in New York on March 4, was asked about the status of the club — a week after Chelsea booked a €407million (£342m) pre-tax deficit for the 2024-25 season, per UEFA data — the highest pre-tax loss in English football.

A club source told The Athletic that this was not reflective of the club’s underlying operating performance or how finances would look for current and future seasons, with last season reflecting a tidying-up of historic issues.

Those worsened the bottom line figure but Chelsea still lost a significant sum before player sales last season, and their business model appears heavily reliant on generating consistently strong profits from transfer dealings.

Feliciano was asked about the loss by event moderator moderator Davide Scigliuzzo, and whether it was a case of “having to spend a lot of money to make a lot of money” with a “rough ride” in sporting results.

Puerto Rican-born American businessman Feliciano highlighted Chelsea’s triumphs in last season’s Conference League and Club World Cup, while qualifying for this season’s Champions League.

“Arsenal hasn’t won in 20 years that I have checked, or maybe they won something, but anyway — we just won two trophies,” said Feliciano.

Feliciano, who alongside Eghbali sits on Chelsea’s board of directors, added: “If you own a sports club, you have to understand that you’re a steward of something much broader, and the impact on the community is much broader than just a business or just a sport.

“We take very seriously that Chelsea has been a top six (team) in the Premier League and we intend to not only stay there, but to compete for trophies every year.

“We intend to win the Premier League soon. I think we have put in place a much more sustainable system in terms of players and development, that I think is yielding results right now.”

Since taking over at Chelsea in 2022, BlueCo’s recruitment has focused on signing young players from around the world on long-term contracts.

Chelsea have the youngest Premier League squad when weighted by minutes played, and have multiple youngsters at other clubs who are either on loan or have reached pre-agreements to join the club side this summer.

Chelsea have spent an estimated £1.8bn ($2.42bn) on incoming signings in transfer windows since BlueCo took over, though they have also made significant player sales. For example, the club raised around £300m from outgoing transfers last summer.

The club were fined by UEFA, European football’s governing body, in July 2025 and placed under a spending restriction after they were found to have breached the governing body’s football earnings and squad cost rules.

Chelsea are currently fifth in the Premier League table, ahead of sixth-placed Liverpool on goal difference and three points behind Aston Villa in fourth. A top-five finish would be enough to qualify for next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a very tough league, the toughest league in the world,” Feliciano said. “We’re fighting to be in that top four or five with names like Liverpool, Villa, (Manchester) United, and I think we’re going to do well.”
